text: When a trader swaps against a pool, they're trading against reserves that liquidity providers deposited. Every fee they pay flows back to those providers, represented by a token that's the subject of this lesson.

Deposit 5 ETH and 10,000 USDC into a 100 ETH / 200,000 USDC pool with 1,000 LP tokens outstanding — 5 percent of each reserve. The pool mints you 50 new LP tokens, now 4.76 percent of the new 1,050-token total.
Every trade pays a fee that stays inside the reserves, so k grows slightly with every trade. Your share percentage doesn't change, but the pool it's a share of keeps getting bigger.

The pool's ratio of the two assets moves with every trade. Redeem your LP tokens later and you get back the current ratio, not your original deposit ratio — the pool mechanically sold some of your ETH the same way it would for any trader.
LP tokens are a proportional claim that grows with fees but rebalances with price. Next up: putting a number on that rebalancing cost — impermanent loss.
